name: json-schema-preview
description: Preview JSON Schema documents inside VSCode.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Rendering a preview runs the json-schema-for-humans Python tool, optionally using a workspace-provided config file. The preview is disabled in untrusted workspaces; validation, schema binding, and inference remain available.

virtualWorkspaces.description: The extension shells out to a local Python interpreter and reads/writes files on disk, neither of which is available in virtual workspaces.

jsonschema.preview.autoOpen.markdownDescription: Automatically open the preview panel when a JSON Schema file is opened or becomes the active editor.

jsonschema.preview.liveUpdate.markdownDescription: Refresh the preview as you type (debounced). The preview panel must already be open.

jsonschema.preview.liveUpdateDelay.markdownDescription: Milliseconds to wait after the last keystroke before the live preview refreshes.

jsonschema.preview.syncScroll.markdownDescription: Keep the preview panel and the schema editor's scroll position in sync — scrolling either one moves the other to the matching position. The preview panel must already be open.

enumDescriptions: Use json-schema-for-humans (Python) when available; fall back to the built-in renderer otherwise.
Always use the built-in dependency-free renderer; never invoke Python (no interpreter probe or install prompt).
jsonschema.preview.renderer.markdownDescription: Which engine renders the schema preview. `auto` prefers the richer `json-schema-for-humans` (Python) output; `builtin` forces the extension's dependency-free renderer so no Python is required.

jsonschema.preview.renderTimeout.markdownDescription: Milliseconds to wait for the `json-schema-for-humans` render subprocess before it is killed and an error page is shown. Values below 1000 ms are clamped.

jsonschema.remoteFetchTimeout.markdownDescription: Milliseconds to wait for an outbound remote-schema HTTP request before it is aborted. Values below 1000 ms are clamped.

jsonschema.refGraph.maxDepth.markdownDescription: When resolving external `$ref`s in the **$ref dependency graph** view (opt-in, prompted per invocation), how many documents deep to fetch and follow further refs before showing the remainder as unfetched endpoint nodes. Values below 1 are clamped.

jsonschema.workspaceValidation.maxFiles.markdownDescription: Maximum number of files the **Validate Workspace** command scans. When the workspace has more matching files, the run is truncated and the report notes it.

enumDescriptions: Never revalidate a locally cached schema automatically; use the Refresh Schema Cache command.
Revalidate a cached schema when a data file bound to it becomes the active editor (at most once per schema per session).
Revalidate a cached schema at most once every 24 hours, checked lazily when a bound file is activated.
jsonschema.cache.autoRefresh.markdownDescription: Automatically revalidate locally cached schemas against their origin using conditional (`ETag` / `Last-Modified`) requests. A `304 Not Modified` response leaves the cache untouched; failures are silent and the cached copy keeps serving IntelliSense.

jsonschema.catalog.useSchemaStore.markdownDescription: Include the public [SchemaStore](https://www.schemastore.org) catalog in the **Bind Schema… → Browse catalog…** picker.

jsonschema.catalog.sources.markdownDescription: Additional schema-catalog URLs in the SchemaStore catalog format (`{ "schemas": [{ "name", "description", "url", "fileMatch" }] }`). Private catalogs are fetched with the credentials configured via **Configure Schema Authentication…**.

jsonschema.lint.enabled.markdownDescription: Report schema-quality diagnostics (missing `description`/`$schema`, unknown keywords, duplicate enums, …) on JSON Schema files.

jsonschema.lint.rules.markdownDescription: Per-rule severity overrides for schema linting. Map a rule id to `off`, `hint`, `info`, or `warning`. Rule ids: `no-unknown-keywords`, `require-schema-declaration`, `require-root-id`, `require-descriptions`, `explicit-additional-properties`, `no-duplicate-enum`, `no-empty-required`, `valid-examples`, `valid-default`.

jsonschema.config.markdownDescription: Configuration for the `json-schema-for-humans` renderer, as an alternative to a committed `.json-schema-preview-config.json` file — see [Preview Configuration](https://samdidos.github.io/vscode-json-schema-preview/guide/configuration) for the precedence rules between the two (the file always wins when both are present). Can be set at User, Workspace, or Workspace Folder scope; a folder/workspace value always overrides a user value. Use **JSON Schema: Configure Preview** to jump straight to the setting in the scope of your choice. All [json-schema-for-humans options](https://github.com/coveooss/json-schema-for-humans#configuration) are accepted — the properties below are just the well-known ones.

template_name.description: The built-in template used to render the documentation.

show_toc.description: Whether to render a table of contents.

expand_buttons.description: Add an "Expand all" / "Collapse all" button at the top of the documentation.

show_breadcrumbs.description: For each property, show its relative place in the schema.

collapse_long_descriptions.description: Show only the beginning of a long description, with a "Read more" button.

collapse_long_examples.description: Collapse long examples, with a "Show" button.

link_to_reused_ref.description: Replace repeated $ref occurrences with anchor links to the first occurrence.

deprecated_from_description.description: Mark a property as deprecated when its description contains "[Deprecated".

default_from_description.description: Extract a property's default value from a "[Default `value`]" marker in its description.

description_is_markdown.description: Render descriptions as Markdown (HTML outputs only).

description_safe_mode.description: How HTML tags inside Markdown descriptions are handled (HTML outputs only).

examples_as_yaml.description: Display examples as YAML instead of JSON.

with_footer.description: Whether to show the footer linking to the json-schema-for-humans repo.

footer_show_time.description: Whether the footer displays the generation time.

custom_template_path.description: Path to a custom Jinja2 template file.

jsonschema.ai.enabled.markdownDescription: Enable AI-assisted authoring (draft descriptions, explain a finding, draft or enrich a schema, generate realistic sample data). **Off by default.** When on, the commands you run send the schema, value or diff they operate on — plus the file's base name — to the language model you have configured in VS Code, through the editor's own Language Model API. This extension ships no model, no API key and no provider endpoint, collects no telemetry, and sends nothing on its own: every request follows a command you invoked. Everything a model produces is verified against the schema engines (parse, Ajv compile, lint, sample) before it is offered, and nothing is written to a file without a preview. See the [AI assistance guide](https://samdidos.github.io/vscode-json-schema-preview/guide/ai).

jsonschema.ai.maxAttempts.markdownDescription: How many times an AI command retries when its result fails verification, feeding the concrete failures back each time. After the last attempt the result is shown explicitly marked unverified, never silently.

enumDescriptions: Only validate when you run JSON Schema: Validate This File.
Re-validate on save when the file has an explicit binding (inline $schema or a settings binding).
Also re-validate on save when VS Code resolves a schema for the file natively (the "(auto)" state).
jsonschema.validation.onSave.markdownDescription: Re-validate a data file when it is saved. Automatic runs are silent — diagnostics only, no notifications — and never fetch an uncached remote schema, so saving is never blocked on the network. This covers YAML, TOML, JSONL and authenticated schemas, which VS Code's own language servers do not validate live.

jsonschema.compat.codeLens.markdownDescription: Show a CodeLens on a schema's first line counting the breaking changes against its Git `HEAD` version. Uses the same classifier as **Diff Against Baseline**; computed in the background so typing is never blocked.

walkthroughs.title: Get started with JSON Schema Preview
walkthroughs.description: Preview, validate and work with JSON Schemas — including private ones — without leaving the editor.

steps.title: Read a schema as documentation
steps.description:
Open a JSON Schema and press the eye icon (or $(keyboard) Ctrl+K V) to render it as navigable documentation beside the editor.
[Open the guide](https://samdidos.github.io/vscode-json-schema-preview/guide/)

steps.title: Bind a schema and validate your data
steps.description:
Bind a JSON, YAML, JSONL or TOML data file to a schema, then validate it — errors land in the Problems panel with quick fixes.
[Command reference](https://samdidos.github.io/vscode-json-schema-preview/guide/commands)

steps.title: Start from data you already have
steps.description:
Generate a schema from an existing document, then generate sample data or typed code back out of it.
[Command reference](https://samdidos.github.io/vscode-json-schema-preview/guide/commands)

steps.title: Use a schema behind authentication
steps.description:
The differentiator most people miss: authenticate against GitHub, Artifactory or any HTTPS endpoint and cache the schema so IntelliSense works too.
[Authentication guide](https://samdidos.github.io/vscode-json-schema-preview/guide/authentication)

languageModelTools.name: jsonschema_validate
languageModelTools.displayName: Validate a JSON, YAML, JSONL or TOML data file against a JSON Schema and return the errors with their line numbers
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Validate a JSON, YAML, JSONL or TOML data file against a JSON Schema and return the errors with their line numbers. Use this instead of judging validity by reading the documents.

dataFile.description: Path to the data file to validate.

schemaFile.description: Path to the JSON Schema to validate against.

languageModelTools.name: jsonschema_lint
languageModelTools.displayName: Report schema-quality findings for a JSON Schema file: unknown keywords, missing descriptions, duplicate enum values, examples and defaults that contradict their own subschema
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Report schema-quality findings for a JSON Schema file: unknown keywords, missing descriptions, duplicate enum values, examples and defaults that contradict their own subschema.

schemaFile.description: Path to the JSON Schema to lint.

languageModelTools.name: jsonschema_diff
languageModelTools.displayName: Compare two versions of a JSON Schema and return a backward-compatibility verdict plus every classified change
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Compare two versions of a JSON Schema and return a backward-compatibility verdict plus every classified change. Use this to decide whether a schema change is breaking — do not infer it from the diff text.

strict.description: Also treat changes the classifier cannot prove safe as blocking.

languageModelTools.name: jsonschema_bundle
languageModelTools.displayName: Flatten a multi-file schema into one self-contained document, either bundling external refs into $defs or dereferencing them inline
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Flatten a multi-file schema into one self-contained document, either bundling external refs into $defs or dereferencing them inline.

dereference.description: Inline ref targets instead of collecting them into $defs.

languageModelTools.name: jsonschema_infer
languageModelTools.displayName: Infer a JSON Schema from an existing data file (JSON, JSONC, JSONL, YAML or TOML)
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Infer a JSON Schema from an existing data file (JSON, JSONC, JSONL, YAML or TOML). Use this to bootstrap a schema from real documents.

dataFile.description: Path to the data file to infer from.

languageModelTools.name: jsonschema_sample
languageModelTools.displayName: Generate a valid example instance from a JSON Schema
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Generate a valid example instance from a JSON Schema. The output is validated against the schema before being returned.

languageModelTools.name: jsonschema_coverage
languageModelTools.displayName: Report which properties a schema declares that the given data files never exercise — the unused-in-data surface of a contract
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Report which properties a schema declares that the given data files never exercise — the unused-in-data surface of a contract.

dataFiles.description: One or more data files to measure coverage from.

languageModelTools.name: jsonschema_test
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Run declarative schema test suites (*.schema.test.json), which pin the documents a schema must accept and must reject. Use this to check a schema change against its contract.

scripts.test:e2e: npm run compile && playwright test --config playwright.e2e.config.ts
scripts.test:integration: npm run compile && tsc -p tsconfig.integration.json && node ./out/test/integration/runTest.js
scripts.generate:assets: npm run test:e2e && npm run make-gifs && npm run make-showcase-gif
